target.title: fix(supervisor): suppress unhandled stream errors on child stdout/stderr
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a supervised child process could crash OpenClaw if stdout or stderr emitted an error after spawn but before the supervisor registered output subscribers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The child adapter now installs exactly one stream-lifetime error guard on stdout and stderr during adapter construction. Subscriber registration remains responsible only for decoding data; existing stream `close` handlers continue to own decoder flush and Windows drain completion.

## User Impact

Early child output-stream failures no longer escape as unhandled Node `error` events. Repeated output subscriptions do not accumulate redundant permanent error listeners, and process wait behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts` (19 passed).
- The test emits errors before output registration, verifies one listener after repeated subscriptions, and proves Windows `wait()` settles only after stream close.
- Real Node child-pipe probe confirmed a destroyed output source emits `error` then `close`.
- `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview reported no accepted or actionable findings.
- Exact prepared head: `a968528d469c3b4e1ca1b7701b84854d9f92160b`.
